body.title: fix(static): normalize indexNames joining to prevent double slash at root
body.body:
Resolves #1584

### Description

In `src/utils/static.ts`, `idSearchPaths` currently builds candidate asset IDs with `${id}${suffix}`.

Because `originalId` for root `GET /` is `"/"`:
- Default `indexNames: ["/index.html"]`: Requesting root `GET /` produces candidate ID `"//index.html"` (an invalid double-slash path that fails lookups against canonical asset maps or storage systems).
- Relative `indexNames: ["index.html"]`: Requesting a subfolder like `GET /docs` produces `"/docsindex.html"` (missing the path separator).

This patch normalizes the join boundary in `idSearchPaths` so that:
- Any leading slashes on index names are stripped before joining.
- If `id` is `"/"`, the root index becomes `"/index.html"`.
- If `id` is a subpath like `"/docs"`, the directory index becomes `"/docs/index.html"`.

### Checklist
- [x] Code passes `pnpm lint`
- [x] Code passes `pnpm test`
- [x] Automated tests added covering root `/`, subpaths, and both leading/non-leading slash `indexNames`

  * Fixed static index-file resolution for the site root and subdirectories. Index files are now found whether their configured names include a leading slash or not, and subdirectory requests resolve correctly with or without a trailing slash.

body.title: docs: fix file paths in static assets example
body.body:
Resolves #1578

The "Read files" example mounts the handler at `/public/**`, but `serveStatic` passes the full request path as `id` (e.g. `/public/index.html`). So `join("public", id)` looks for `public/public/index.html` and every request returns 404. The text also says to open `http://localhost:3000`, which isn't matched by `/public/**`.

Changes:
- Strip the `/public` prefix from `id` before joining it with the directory.
- Point readers to `http://localhost:3000/public/`, after the full example.

I checked both versions against h3 2.0.2 with a `public/index.html` file:

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | 404 | 404 (outside the mount, expected) |
| `/public/` | 404 | 200 |
| `/public/index.html` | 404 | 200 |

* **Documentation**
  * Updated the static assets example to show creating `public/index.html` before opening `/public/` in a browser.
  * Clarified that `/public` is removed from request paths before they’re used to read files or look up file metadata.
